question: What is the biggest danger of carelessly throwing away used sharps?

options.A: Blockage of municipal drainage and sewage pipes
options.B: Transmission of blood infections through accidental pricks
options.C: Creation of unpleasant odors in hospital wards
options.D: Attraction of rodents and insects to the facility

explanation: A stray needle can pierce the skin and directly introduce infections like Hepatitis or HIV into a healthcare worker's bloodstream. Be careful out there! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of using motivational interviewing with a patient?

options.A: Focusing only on laboratory test results
options.B: Giving the patient a strict list of forbidden foods
options.C: Telling the patient exactly what will happen if they fail
options.D: Helping the patient find their own reasons to change

explanation: Brilliant! Motivational interviewing is about having a supportive chat that helps patients discover their own inner drive to live healthier. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h4)

question: Why might a doctor prescribe a topical NSAID gel instead of pills for sore joints?

options.A: It provides localized relief with fewer systemic side effects
options.B: It permanently restores lost joint cartilage
options.C: It cures the disease much faster than pills
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for physical therapy

explanation: Spot on! Putting medicine right on the sore joint gives great relief while protecting your stomach and kidneys from the side effects of pills.

question: How can eating a lot of heavily processed foods affect a patient's health over time?

options.A: They cause immediate paralysis in the limbs
options.B: They often contain excess sodium, sugar, and unhealthy additives
options.C: They prevent the body from digesting water
options.D: They automatically carry dangerous viral infections

explanation: Heavy processing often sneaks in loads of salt, sugar, and preservatives which are big drivers of chronic conditions like high blood pressure and diabetes.

question: Why must sublingual nitroglycerin tablets be stored in a special dark, airtight glass bottle?

options.A: Glass containers prevent the pills from melting in warm weather.
options.B: Light turns the medication into a dangerous poison.
options.C: The medication loses potency easily when exposed to light and air.
options.D: Dark bottles keep the tablets from sticking together.

explanation: Spot on! Nitroglycerin loses its strength quickly if light and air get to it, so the special bottle keeps it potent.

question: Which piece of information is NOT strictly required on a medication label immediately after dilution?

options.A: The exact dose and concentration prepared
options.B: The patient's favorite hobby or pastime
options.C: The generic or brand name of the drug
options.D: The initials of the nurse who mixed it

explanation: Personal hobbies are irrelevant to medication safety. Labels require identification of the drug, dose, patient, time, and preparer. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h6)

question: Which of these details is least important to write down in a standard family planning follow-up note?

options.A: Blood pressure and vital health changes
options.B: Current contraceptive method and compliance
options.C: The brand of pen used by the nurse to write the chart
options.D: Side effects discussed and counseling provided

explanation: We only care about clinical facts! The brand of pen has nothing to do with patient health or safe care continuity.

question: Which two major bone fractures are notorious for causing massive internal bleeding?

options.A: Pelvis and femur
options.B: Phalanges and carpals
options.C: Clavicle and scapula
options.D: Radius and ulna

explanation: Large bones like the pelvis and femur are packed with blood vessels and bone marrow. When they break, they can bleed significantly inside the body before anyone even notices.

question: Why must internal waste transport trolleys always be covered when moving through the hospital?

options.A: To make the trolleys move faster down the ramp
options.B: To keep the trash bags cool under direct sunlight
options.C: To hide unpleasant sights from the hospital visitors
options.D: To prevent accidental spills and exposure along hospital corridors

explanation: You nailed it! Covering the trolley stops items from falling out and protects patients and staff walking in the hallways.

question: A nurse is opening a new file for a client requesting an injectable contraceptive. Which finding must be documented under medical history before administering the drug?

options.A: The exact time the client woke up today
options.B: Any history of chronic conditions like hypertension
options.C: The distance from the client's house to the market
options.D: The client's favorite brand of soap

explanation: Medical history includes chronic illnesses because conditions like high blood pressure influence which contraceptive methods are safe to prescribe. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h2)

question: Which group of worms are flat, ribbon-like, and segmented?

options.A: Trematodes
options.B: Cestodes
options.C: Protozoa
options.D: Nematodes

explanation: Great try! Cestodes are our tapeworms—easily recognized by their flat, segmented ribbon-like bodies.

question: Why is true, informed consent impossible when dealing with early or forced marriages involving minors?

options.A: Government laws automatically invalidate all youth marriages
options.B: Minors lack the developmental maturity to fully grasp lifelong consequences
options.C: Families rarely hold traditional wedding ceremonies for youths
options.D: Religious leaders always forbid young people from marrying

explanation: Spot on! True consent means fully understanding a major life decision. Young minds are still developing and cannot grasp these lifelong impacts yet.

question: Why do nurses monitor blood inflammatory markers like ESR and CRP in osteomyelitis patients?

options.A: To measure the exact amount of calcium left in the bone shaft
options.B: To track how well the body is responding to treatment over time
options.C: To prove that the infection started from a dental cavity
options.D: To determine whether the patient needs an immediate blood transfusion

explanation: ESR and CRP go up when there's inflammation and drop back down as the patient gets better. They are great tools to see if our treatments are working!

question: What does a nurse typically see during an otoscopic exam of a patient with acute ear infection (otitis media)?

options.A: A clear, translucent eardrum with a sharp cone of light
options.B: A dark perforated hole with dry flaky skin inside the canal
options.C: A bulging, bright red tympanic membrane with obscured landmarks
options.D: A completely pale, flat membrane with prominent bone outlines

explanation: When pus builds up behind the eardrum from an infection, it pushes the drum outward and turns it very red, hiding the normal landmarks.

question: Which plant is the natural source of the heart medication digoxin?

options.A: Opium poppy plant
options.B: Digitalis or foxglove
options.C: Deadly nightshade
options.D: Cinchona tree bark

explanation: Digoxin comes from the pretty foxglove plant! It's a classic example of how nature helps us treat heart conditions.

question: What is the patient expected to do during the 45 to 60 minute waiting period after getting the tracer injection?

options.A: Rest quietly in a comfortable, low-stimulus room without talking or moving.
options.B: Eat a high-protein meal to stabilize blood sugar levels before scanning.
options.C: Walk briskly around the hospital corridor to pump blood through the body.
options.D: Perform deep breathing exercises and arm stretches to relax muscles.

explanation: Correct! If the patient talks, reads, or moves around too much, their brain and muscles will burn glucose and steal the tracer away from the organs the doctor actually wants to check.

question: Which group of occupational lung diseases is caused by inhaling mineral dusts like silica and asbestos?

options.A: Pneumoconiosis
options.B: Simple Bronchitis
options.C: Occupational Asthma
options.D: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis

explanation: Pneumoconiosis is the medical term for fibrotic lung diseases caused by the accumulation of mineral dusts in the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why must nurses look at the whole person—not just physical symptoms—when caring for palliative patients?

options.A: Physical pain never occurs without accompanying fever.
options.B: Physical symptoms are often worsened by emotional and spiritual distress.
options.C: Medications only work if the patient is sleeping soundly.
options.D: Lab tests can detect all forms of human suffering.

explanation: Everything is connected! When a patient is worried, scared, or spiritually troubled, their physical pain often feels much worse. Holistic care means healing the whole person.

question: A patient arrives with a deep dog puncture on their hand. After checking the ABCs, what should the nurse assess first?

options.A: The patient's current insurance and employment details
options.B: Distal pulses, motor function, and finger sensation
options.C: Whether the patient prefers oral or intravenous medication
options.D: The exact monetary value of any damaged clothing

explanation: Always check circulation, movement, and feeling early on! Deep punctures can easily cause hidden damage to nearby blood vessels and tendons.

question: What is the main job of an umbilical cord clamp?

options.A: To hold the sewing needle steady during repairs
options.B: To safely stop blood flow through the cut cord stump
options.C: To gently clear mucus from the newborn's nose
options.D: To clamp blood vessels inside the mother's uterus

explanation: Cord clamps lock tightly onto the baby's cord right after it's cut to keep the baby safe from any bleeding.

question: Which professional group is NOT part of the healthcare team managing suspected elder abuse?

options.A: Home healthcare nurses
options.B: Astronaut training coordinators
options.C: Medical social workers
options.D: Primary care physicians

explanation: Rocket science has no place here—multidisciplinary teams for elder care involve nurses, doctors, and social workers!

question: A patient tells you they drink alcohol 'only socially.' What is your best next step?

options.A: Accept the vague answer and move on to the next topic
options.B: Document that the patient denies all alcohol consumption
options.C: Assume the patient is hiding a severe addiction disorder
options.D: Ask specifically how many drinks they consume per week

explanation: Great thinking! 'Socially' means different things to everyone, so getting a specific number helps you understand their actual intake.

question: A pregnant client at 32 weeks gestation reports a sudden severe headache and blurred vision. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Suggest she drink more water and take a mild over-the-counter pain reliever
options.B: Notify the primary care provider immediately to evaluate for preeclampsia
options.C: Reassure her that these are normal symptoms of increased blood volume
options.D: Advise her to lie flat on her back for an hour to relieve eye strain

explanation: Severe headaches and visual disturbances are cardinal signs of gestational hypertension or preeclampsia, which require urgent medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h6)

question: What direct action allows a muscle fiber to return to its normal resting length?

options.A: Fresh ATP binds directly to the actin filaments
options.B: Motor neurons release more potassium into the sarcoplasm
options.C: Calcium ions are pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum
options.D: Tropomyosin permanently detaches from the Z-lines

explanation: When the calcium is safely sucked back into storage, the blocking proteins snap back into place, letting the muscle rest and relax. You're crushing this! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h7)

question: Which major protein in the blood plasma binds heavily to many circulating medications?

options.A: Globulin
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Fibrinogen
options.D: Albumin

explanation: Albumin is the most abundant protein floating in your plasma. It acts like a taxi service, binding to many drug molecules as they travel through the bloodstream.

question: Which muscle group forms the main support sling at the base of the pelvis?

options.A: Obturator internus
options.B: Iliopsoas
options.C: Levator ani
options.D: Rectus abdominis

explanation: You've got this! The levator ani muscles act like a sturdy muscular sling that keeps all your pelvic organs safely in place.

question: What is the main reason doctors order blood screening tests for a patient exposed to unsafe injections?

options.A: To measure the exact amount of muscle mass in the limbs
options.B: To test for common food allergies and dietary sensitivities
options.C: To determine how quickly the patient's kidneys filter water
options.D: To check for the presence of blood-borne viral infections

explanation: Serological screening helps us catch antibodies or antigens for viruses like HIV or Hepatitis early, so the patient can get timely support.

question: Why is noting the exact time of death so crucial for the healthcare team?

options.A: It determines how long the bed stays empty
options.B: It dictates the cost of the hospital bill
options.C: It starts legal and administrative timelines
options.D: It proves the nurse followed hospital policy

explanation: Spot on! The recorded time marks the official start for all the legal paperwork, death certificates, and hospital records that follow.

question: Why must a nurse always clean an instrument before disinfecting it?

options.A: To sterilize the equipment without using heat or gas
options.B: To dry the medical instrument so it does not rust
options.C: To remove organic matter that can block chemical disinfectants
options.D: To instantly kill all bacterial spores present on the surface

explanation: Think of dirt or dried blood as a shield for germs! Cleaning washes away that organic barrier so your disinfectant can actually reach and kill the bacteria.

question: A patient's right thumb starts twitching, then the whole arm shakes, and soon the entire body is involved with a loss of consciousness. What is this called?

options.A: A primary generalized myoclonic twitch
options.B: A benign febrile convulsion
options.C: Focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizure
options.D: A purely generalized absence seizure

explanation: You nailed it! Starting in one spot ('focal') and spreading to take over the whole brain ('bilateral') describes this exact progression.

question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of kwashiorkor?

options.A: Severe muscle wasting with no body fat at all
options.B: Rapid overgrowth of the long bones
options.C: Generalized pitting edema and skin changes
options.D: An extremely high fever with sudden seizures

explanation: Kwashiorkor happens when a child lacks enough protein. A classic giveaway is swelling (edema) in the body and noticeable skin changes.

question: What is a major advantage of using topical medications over oral medications?

options.A: They require no prior skin assessment or cleaning before application
options.B: They completely eliminate the possibility of any allergic reaction
options.C: They avoid gastrointestinal distress and first-pass liver metabolism
options.D: They absorb at the exact same predictable speed on every part of the body

explanation: Topical drugs bypass the stomach and liver breakdown cycle, making them great for patients experiencing severe nausea or vomiting. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h5)

question: How does vascular dementia primarily develop, setting it apart from Alzheimer's disease?

options.A: It only affects physical movement without touching memory
options.B: It is triggered strictly by nutritional deficiencies in old age
options.C: It is caused by reduced blood flow to the brain from problems like strokes
options.D: It develops entirely from sudden viral infections of the nervous tissue

explanation: Spot on! Vascular dementia happens when blood supply to the brain is blocked or reduced—often due to tiny strokes—starving brain cells of oxygen.

question: Why is keeping things confidential so vital when caring for teenagers?

options.A: It stops teenagers from needing any physical examinations at all
options.B: It guarantees that the adolescent will never experience an infection
options.C: It encourages teenagers to truthfully disclose sensitive health and lifestyle information
options.D: It is a legal requirement that prevents parents from ever knowing their child is sick

explanation: Teens worry about being judged. When we promise confidentiality, we build the trust they need to open up and tell us the truth about their health.

question: How do the internal and external urethral sphincters differ from each other?

options.A: The internal sphincter is smooth muscle while the external sphincter is skeletal muscle.
options.B: The internal sphincter is voluntary while the external sphincter is entirely involuntary.
options.C: Both sphincters are made entirely of involuntary smooth muscle.
options.D: Both sphincters are made exclusively of skeletal muscle fibers.

explanation: Think of it this way: the internal sphincter works automatically (smooth muscle), while the external one is under your conscious control so you can hold it (skeletal muscle). Great job!

question: At what Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score do doctors usually decide to insert an artificial airway (intubation) to protect the patient?

options.A: 8 or lower
options.B: 12 or lower
options.C: 15 exactly
options.D: 3 only

explanation: Remember the golden rule in trauma: 'less than 8, intubate!' A score of 8 or lower means the patient can no longer protect their own airway.

question: Why do nurses need to know emergency devices very well before a crisis happens?

options.A: To prevent equipment theft in the ward
options.B: To ensure fast and effective action during high-stress moments
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: To avoid having to document patient care tasks

explanation: Spot on! In an emergency, knowing your tools right away helps you act fast and save precious time. You are doing great! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why does a reentry circuit cause an arrhythmia?

options.A: It forces the heart muscle cells to permanently stop receiving oxygen
options.B: It traps an electrical signal in a looping pathway that causes rapid contractions
options.C: It immediately destroys the natural pacemaker cells in the right atrium
options.D: It completely blocks all electrical impulses from leaving the sinoatrial node

explanation: A reentry circuit occurs when an electrical wave gets stuck traveling in a circle, constantly re-stimulating the heart tissue to beat too fast. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h1)

question: How does a nurse's role in a primary health center usually differ from working in a big teaching hospital?

options.A: Primary nurses work with greater independence in community wellness and prevention
options.B: Tertiary nurses never administer medications or check vital signs
options.C: Primary nurses only perform complex open-heart surgeries daily
options.D: Tertiary nurses do not require any formal nursing education

explanation: At a primary health center, nurses often run clinics independently, focusing heavily on health promotion, immunizations, and spotting community health issues early.

question: Why does the trigone area of the bladder stay smooth instead of forming folds when empty?

options.A: It lacks any mucous membrane lining completely.
options.B: It is made of rigid bone-like cartilage tissue.
options.C: Its mucous membrane is firmly attached to the muscle layer.
options.D: It stays permanently stretched by constant fluid pressure.

explanation: You nailed it! While the rest of the bladder wrinkles up (forming rugae) when empty, the trigone is tightly anchored down so it stays nice and smooth.

question: What is a common healthcare habit among many patients in Nigeria regarding traditional and modern hospital care?

options.A: Using both traditional and orthodox systems, sometimes concurrently
options.B: Using exclusively orthodox hospitals and completely ignoring local herbs
options.C: Relying entirely on foreign imported medications
options.D: Consulting spiritual healers only after death has occurred

explanation: Correct! Many people naturally blend traditional remedies with modern hospital treatments in their daily lives.

question: If local surveys show an increase in unmet family planning needs among teenagers, what is the best nursing action?

options.A: Close the adolescent clinic to prevent community backlash
options.B: Establish youth-friendly reproductive health education and confidential counseling
options.C: Assume the survey data is incorrect and take no action
options.D: Report the teenagers to local law enforcement authorities immediately

explanation: Teens need a safe, judgment-free space to ask questions. Setting up youth-friendly, confidential clinics helps them get the right guidance without fear.

question: A nurse has three different crushed pill medications to give a patient through a PEG tube. What is the correct way to administer them?

options.A: Mix all three crushed pills together in one large syringe of water
options.B: Give each medication separately with a water flush between them
options.C: Crush them together and push them down the dry tube all at once
options.D: Dissolve the pills directly into the hanging bag of liquid formula

explanation: Medications must never be mixed together in a single syringe to avoid drug interactions and severe tube blockage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h6)

question: What major global health crisis drove the rapid development of early mechanical ventilation?

options.A: The polio epidemics of the mid-20th century
options.B: The 1918 influenza pandemic across Europe
options.C: Major outbreaks of cholera in crowded cities
options.D: The rapid rise of severe traumatic road accidents

explanation: The polio epidemics caused widespread respiratory paralysis, forcing hospitals to find mechanical ways to help patients breathe. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h2)

question: You notice a patient's GCS score dropped from 14 to 10 over two hours. What should you do right away?

options.A: Document the score in the chart and leave the room for a break.
options.B: Administer a strong sleeping pill to calm the restless patient.
options.C: Wait another four hours to see if the patient wakes up naturally.
options.D: Notify the healthcare provider immediately and report the neurological decline.

explanation: A dropping GCS score is an urgent red flag! Any sudden decline in a patient's alertness means you must alert the doctor right away.

question: What is the main purpose of tracking indicators in a PAC monitoring and evaluation system?

options.A: To publicly expose staff members who make clinical mistakes
options.B: To calculate individual nurses' salaries based on procedure counts
options.C: To reduce the total number of patients visiting the health facility
options.D: To measure service performance, track outcomes, and guide quality improvement

explanation: Monitoring and evaluation helps managers see what is working well and where gaps exist, so the facility can continuously improve patient care.

question: What creates the direct pathway for spreading disease during an unsafe injection?

options.A: Inhaling medication droplets while prepping a syringe
options.B: A contaminated needle breaking the skin and entering circulation
options.C: Swallowing oral tablets without enough water
options.D: Touching a sealed medication package with bare hands

explanation: Spot on! Injections bypass your skin's natural defense barrier, meaning any germs on a dirty needle go straight into the patient's tissues and bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h4)

question: Your patient's GCS score keeps dropping over the last two hours. What should this trend tell you immediately?

options.A: Normal tiredness at the end of the day
options.B: A minor hearing loss developing in the patient
options.C: Worsening neurological status and potential brain swelling
options.D: A temporary reaction to hospital food

explanation: A falling GCS score is a serious warning sign. It means brain function is declining and you must act fast!

question: What is a major nursing responsibility while an EPS is actively happening?

options.A: Monitoring continuous heart rhythms and blood pressure
options.B: Performing surgical closure of the blood vessel access site
options.C: Interpreting the final medical billing codes for the procedure
options.D: Personally advancing the catheter electrodes into the heart

explanation: You are the patient's eyes and ears! Keeping a close eye on the monitors and vitals keeps the patient safe while the team works inside the heart.

question: A woman carrying twins at 38 weeks asks to have her babies at home. What should you tell her?

options.A: Suggest waiting until labor is well established before deciding
options.B: Explain that multiple pregnancies require hospital care due to higher risks
options.C: Encourage home birth because twins are common in the community
options.D: Agree to attend the home birth if contractions are mild and regular

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Twin pregnancies carry higher chances of tricky presentations or heavy bleeding, so they truly need the safety of a health facility.

question: A nurse checks a poorly arranged office desk that causes chronic back strain. What kind of hazard is this?

options.A: Biological hazards
options.B: Chemical hazards
options.C: Ergonomic hazards
options.D: Physical hazards

explanation: Ergonomic hazards happen when the workspace or tools do not fit the natural posture and movement of the human body.

question: Why do deep scratches or infections on the cornea take so long to heal?

options.A: Sunlight constantly damages the cornea
options.B: Tears wash away all the healing white blood cells
options.C: The cornea does not have its own blood supply
options.D: Eye germs are immune to normal inflammation

explanation: Correct! Because the cornea has no blood vessels of its own, infection-fighting cells and nutrients have to travel a long way from nearby tissues, slowing down healing.

question: Which lifestyle change helps the most in managing stress incontinence?

options.A: Drinking less than two cups of fluid per day
options.B: Achieving and maintaining a healthy body weight
options.C: Eliminating all forms of physical exercise completely
options.D: Increasing daily intake of carbonated beverages

explanation: Shedding extra pounds takes a huge amount of constant pressure off the pelvic floor muscles. You're doing great!

question: Why is providing respite care so important for family caregivers?

options.A: It cures the caregiver of any risk for developing the genetic disease
options.B: It teaches the patient how to live independently without any help
options.C: It permanently transfers all legal responsibility to the hospital staff
options.D: It gives them temporary relief from care duties to prevent complete burnout

explanation: You're doing fantastic! Respite care offers a much-needed breather so caregivers can rest, recharge, and protect their own health. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h6)

question: A patient is admitted with suspected celiac disease. Which specific blood test does the nurse expect the healthcare provider to order first?

options.A: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA)
options.B: Serum amylase and lipase levels
options.C: Anti-tissue transglutaminase (tTG) antibodies
options.D: Blood urea nitrogen and creatinine

explanation: Serologic antibody testing for anti-tTG is the standard primary screening tool used to detect celiac disease in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h6)

question: Which bacteria is well-known for causing rapid and severe postpartum infections?

options.A: Group A Streptococcus
options.B: Candida albicans
options.C: Lactobacillus acidophilus
options.D: Corynebacterium diphtheriae

explanation: Group A Streptococcus is notorious in midwifery for causing very rapid and severe illness in new mothers. Quick action is always key here!

question: Which part of the brain acts as the body's internal thermostat?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Medulla oblongata
options.D: Thalamus

explanation: The hypothalamus is the specific brain region responsible for monitoring and regulating core body temperature. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is opening the airway the top priority in emergency care?

options.A: It prevents patients from talking too loudly
options.B: Blocked air passages quickly lead to brain death
options.C: It stops internal bone bleeding immediately
options.D: Doctors cannot write prescriptions without it

explanation: Without a clear airway, oxygen cannot reach the brain. Brain cells start dying in minutes without oxygen, so we must clear the airway first!

question: Why is occupational therapy so helpful for patients with chronic joint disorders?

options.A: It provides surgical joint replacement procedures
options.B: It teaches energy-conservation techniques and assistive devices
options.C: It cures the underlying autoimmune malfunction
options.D: It prescribes high-dose corticosteroid injections

explanation: Occupational therapists are wonderful! They teach patients smart ways to protect their joints, save energy, and use handy tools to stay independent.

question: Which device is best for giving tiny amounts of medicine slowly over time, especially for newborns?

options.A: Ambulatory blood warmer
options.B: Gravity drip set
options.C: Large volume pump
options.D: Syringe pump

explanation: Great job! Syringe pumps are brilliant for low volumes because they push the plunger forward in tiny, steady steps.

question: What is the main difference between emission and ejaculation?

options.A: Emission is controlled by parasympathetic nerves, while erection is sympathetic
options.B: Emission involves only the testes, while ejaculation involves the prostate
options.C: Emission moves fluid into the urethra, while ejaculation expels it outward
options.D: Emission happens before puberty, while ejaculation occurs only in adulthood

explanation: Spot on! Emission gathers and moves the fluid into the upper urethra, while ejaculation uses muscle contractions to push it completely out of the body.

question: What is the main difference between drug tolerance and psychological addiction?

options.A: Tolerance happens only in children; addiction happens in adults
options.B: Addiction is caused by paracetamol, tolerance by morphine
options.C: Tolerance means the drug stops working for any condition
options.D: Tolerance is a normal body adjustment needing higher doses, while addiction involves compulsive craving

explanation: Well explained! Tolerance just means your body gets used to a drug over time so you need a bit more for the same effect. Addiction is a complex behavioral drive to use drugs compulsively.

question: What is the best position to place a patient in before you start feeding them?

options.A: Trendelenburg position with feet elevated higher than the head
options.B: High Fowler's position or 90 degrees upright in a chair
options.C: Semi-Fowler's position at a gentle 30-degree angle
options.D: Flat on the back with a small pillow under the neck

explanation: Sitting upright uses gravity to help food go down smoothly and, most importantly, keeps the airway safe from choking.

question: What is the main purpose of occupational health surveillance?

options.A: To punish workers who report feeling sick on the job
options.B: To catch early signs of work-related illness through regular testing
options.C: To calculate the exact salary of every factory worker
options.D: To replace the need for engineering safety barriers

explanation: Surveillance monitors worker health over time so that illnesses can be detected and treated early before causing permanent damage. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: A community health nurse visits a home where a parent recently died from an AIDS-related illness. What is the best first step to take?

options.A: Discharge the family from clinic follow-up to protect patient privacy
options.B: Immediately report the extended family to the police for property grabbing
options.C: Transfer all children to a distant government orphanage home
options.D: Perform a comprehensive assessment of the children's nutritional and social needs

explanation: A complete nursing assessment helps you understand their health, feeding status, and immediate social needs so you can offer the right help. Nursing is all about holistic care!

question: How does Nigeria's strict legal stance on abortion end up hurting maternal health?

options.A: It forces procedures underground, leading to dangerous and secretive practices
options.B: It eliminates the need for contraceptives in rural communities
options.C: It guarantees that all women receive free post-abortion medications
options.D: It encourages traditional birth attendants to learn modern surgery

explanation: Making laws strict doesn't stop abortions; it just drives them underground where unsterile tools and secret methods cause severe complications.

question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator in the ICU?

options.A: To replace the function of the human heart
options.B: To assist or take over the work of breathing
options.C: To increase blood pressure in shock patients
options.D: To cure underlying lung diseases permanently

explanation: Think of the ventilator as an extra pair of lungs! It helps or completely takes over breathing to keep oxygen flowing while the patient's body heals. You've got this!

question: A patient living in a rural home with poor kitchen ventilation uses wood for daily cooking and now has a lasting cough. What is the best primary prevention advice?

options.A: Give them a course of strong oral antibiotics right away
options.B: Recommend using a quick-relief rescue inhaler every day
options.C: Order a chest X-ray to check for tuberculosis
options.D: Advise the family to switch to cleaner cooking fuel and improve kitchen airflow

explanation: Primary prevention stops the problem before it starts or worsens. Fixing indoor smoke exposure removes the root environmental trigger keeping that cough going!

question: What are the two main hormone types found in combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: Prolactin and progestin
options.B: Progesterone and testosterone
options.C: Estrogen and oxytocin
options.D: Estrogen and progestin

explanation: Combined oral contraceptives contain a blend of synthetic estrogen and progestin to prevent pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h1)

question: What should you do with empty blood bags right after a transfusion finishes?

options.A: Throw them into the general municipal waste bin immediately
options.B: Wash them out with soap and return them to the patient bedside
options.C: Burn them in the hospital incinerator within five minutes
options.D: Retain them temporarily according to institutional policy

explanation: Hang onto them for a bit! If the patient shows any delayed reaction, the blood bank might need those empty bags and tubing to run investigation tests.

question: Why should you keep infusion pumps plugged into the wall socket when patients are resting in bed?

options.A: To allow the pump to automatically clean its internal tubing
options.B: To prevent the pump screen from displaying warning messages
options.C: To increase the speed at which medications are delivered
options.D: To preserve the internal battery for times when the patient is moving

explanation: You got it! Keeping it plugged in saves the battery charge for when the patient needs to walk around or go for a test.

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care when using the concept of basic human needs?

options.A: Discharging the patient as quickly as possible
options.B: Focusing on the whole person and their essential requirements
options.C: Treating only the diagnosed disease process
options.D: Managing hospital administrative tasks

explanation: Looking at basic human needs helps nurses care for the entire individual rather than just treating a specific illness. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: What type of language should a nurse use when documenting physical exam findings?

options.A: Vague and generalized terms like 'fine'
options.B: Subjective opinions about the patient's attitude
options.C: Clear, objective, and descriptive language
options.D: Complex poetic metaphors to describe wounds

explanation: Objective descriptions prevent confusion and provide clear facts for other healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h7)

question: Which chemical agent requires a special airing-out (aeration) period because it leaves toxic gas behind?

options.A: Ordinary liquid soap
options.B: Hydrogen peroxide
options.C: Ethylene oxide
options.D: Standard tap water

explanation: Ethylene oxide is a strong sterilizing gas, but items need to sit in a special aeration chamber afterward to clear out lingering toxic fumes.

question: Which concept forms the core foundation of a clean delivery kit?

options.A: The six cleans of childbirth
options.B: Immediate surgical intervention
options.C: Routine administration of heavy IV antibiotics
options.D: Continuous electronic fetal monitoring

explanation: The kit is built directly around ensuring hands, surfaces, perineum, cord tools, cord ties, and baby wraps are completely clean. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why is metoclopramide a big NO-GO for a patient with a confirmed bowel blockage (obstruction)?

options.A: It completely stops the absorption of oral pain medications
options.B: It will neutralize all digestive enzymes in the small intestine
options.C: It causes severe respiratory depression in obstructed patients
options.D: Increasing motility against a blockage can cause bowel perforation

explanation: You got it! Pushing gut movement when there's a physical roadblock can cause the intestine to burst. Always check for obstructions before giving prokinetics!

question: What is a key nursing check to perform after a patient receives IV contrast dye?

options.A: Measuring hourly urine output to confirm total bladder atrophy
options.B: Monitoring for delayed allergic reactions like rash, itching, or breathing difficulty
options.C: Checking for immediate loss of hair color around the injection site
options.D: Assessing for sudden paralysis in the lower extremities

explanation: Allergic reactions to contrast dye can sometimes pop up hours later. Always keep an eye out for hives, itching, or any trouble breathing.

question: A patient has sudden flare-ups of numbness and weakness that completely clear up after a few weeks, followed by long periods of normal health. What pattern is this?

options.A: Secondary progressive
options.B: Relapsing-remitting
options.C: Primary progressive
options.D: Benign transient paresis

explanation: This is the classic 'relapsing-remitting' pattern—clear flare-ups (relapses) followed by periods where the patient recovers and feels fine (remissions).

question: What actually happens inside the body during a Type I allergic reaction to a medication?

options.A: Accumulation of fluid in the peripheral blood vessels
options.B: Mast cell degranulation releasing histamine and other mediators
options.C: Direct toxicity of the drug on the kidney tubules
options.D: Rapid breakdown of red blood cells in the liver

explanation: When antibodies trigger mast cells to burst open and release histamine, it leads to rapid itching, swelling, and trouble breathing.

question: Which bone cells are primarily responsible for breaking down or resorbing bone tissue?

options.A: Osteoblasts
options.B: Chondrocytes
options.C: Osteocytes
options.D: Osteoclasts

explanation: A great trick to remember this: Osteo*clasts* **c**rash or **c**ut down bone! They are the cleanup and remodeling crew that breaks down bone matrix when your body needs to shape or repair it.

question: What do we call a non-living object—like a stethoscope, door handle, or bed sheet—that can pass germs from one person to another?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Vector
options.C: Carrier
options.D: Fomite

explanation: You've got this! Non-living items that carry germs around are called fomites. Think of things like dirty linens or blood pressure cuffs moving microbes from patient to patient.

question: What imaging test is considered the absolute gold standard for spotting a pituitary tumor?

options.A: An ultrasound scan of the blood vessels in the neck
options.B: A plain X-ray picture of the skull from the side
options.C: A standard CT scan of the head without any contrast dye
options.D: An MRI of the brain using contrast dye

explanation: MRI is the best choice because it gives super clear pictures of soft tissues. This lets doctors spot tiny adenomas and see if they are crowding nearby structures like the optic nerves.

question: Which part of a used mask is safe to touch when taking it off?

options.A: The metal nose bridge exterior
options.B: The bottom edge near the chin
options.C: The straps, ties, or ear loops
options.D: The front center filtration panel

explanation: Always grab the straps! The front of the mask holds onto trapped germs and should never be touched directly.

question: A survivor of forced marriage discloses her situation to a nurse in confidence. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Post the details of the case on social media to raise quick awareness
options.B: Advise the patient to return home and obey her spouse to keep the peace
options.C: Maintain confidentiality while safely connecting her with social services and support
options.D: Inform the village elders immediately to resolve the family dispute

explanation: Protecting patient confidentiality and linking them to specialized support networks is critical for their safety and recovery. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h6)

question: In a regular 28-day cycle, when do we usually check serum progesterone to see if ovulation happened?

options.A: Mid-luteal phase around day 21
options.B: During active menstrual bleeding
options.C: Immediately at the end of menses
options.D: On the exact day of ovulation

explanation: You got it! Progesterone peaks after ovulation, making day 21 the sweet spot in a standard cycle to check if ovulation took place.

question: What does the acronym ADL stand for in healthcare?

options.A: Advanced Drug List
options.B: Activities of Daily Living
options.C: Assisted Diet Limitation
options.D: Acute Disease Level

explanation: ADLs stand for Activities of Daily Living, which represent the essential self-care tasks required every day. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h2)

question: Why do symptoms suddenly show up after a quiet incubation phase?

options.A: The number of germs and body damage cross a tipping point
options.B: The immune system completely stops working
options.C: The germs suddenly turn into a completely different species
options.D: Medicines taken by the patient start fighting healthy cells

explanation: Illness only becomes visible when the growing number of germs and tiny injuries finally overwhelm the body's natural defenses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h2)

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for at the very beginning of the SBAR communication tool?

options.A: Solution
options.B: Situation
options.C: Severity
options.D: Symptoms

explanation: Spot on! In SBAR, the first 'S' is for Situation—a quick summary of what is happening right now that made you call or report.

question: Why does a pulmonary shunt cause very low blood oxygen that doesn't easily fix with standard oxygen therapy?

options.A: Excess carbon dioxide blocks the hemoglobin binding sites permanently
options.B: Surfactant production stops completely, causing widespread lung collapse
options.C: Blood bypasses unventilated alveoli, so it never gets oxygen to pick up
options.D: The heart pumps too slowly to push blood through the narrowed pulmonary veins

explanation: Exactly. If blood flows past collapsed or fluid-filled sacs without getting oxygen, adding extra oxygen to room air can't reach that blocked blood! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a community health education program?

options.A: To create unnecessary paperwork for the local government health office
options.B: To punish community members who failed to attend the teaching sessions
options.C: To prove that the nurse is smarter than the people in the village
options.D: To determine if the program achieved its goals and identify areas for improvement

explanation: Correct! Evaluation helps you see what worked well and what you can do better next time.

question: Why do doctors sometimes order a contrast angiogram for someone with severe peripheral vascular disease?

options.A: To map out the exact spot and size of blocked arteries
options.B: To measure electrical signals in the leg muscles
options.C: To see if the patient has high blood pressure overall
options.D: To check how long it takes for a blood sample to clot

explanation: An angiogram uses a special dye to take clear pictures of the blood vessels, acting like a roadmap so doctors can see exactly where the blockages are.

question: What is the big advantage of using open-ended questions?

options.A: They provide quick, exact "yes" or "no" answers
options.B: They encourage the patient to share a detailed narrative
options.C: They eliminate the need for active listening entirely
options.D: They prevent the patient from talking too much

explanation: Spot on! Open questions let patients tell their story in their own words, giving you much better insight.

question: Where should a nurse refer a client who requests a permanent surgical contraceptive method like bilateral tubal ligation?

options.A: To a secondary or tertiary hospital
options.B: To a local patent medicine vendor
options.C: To a primary health post
options.D: To a community outreach market stall

explanation: Surgical procedures require operating theater facilities and specialized personnel usually found at secondary or tertiary hospitals. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h3)

question: How do deep, slow breathing exercises physically help a patient calm down?

options.A: They increase skeletal muscle tension to release trapped toxins
options.B: They permanently block the adrenal glands from producing cortisol
options.C: They flood the bloodstream with extra adrenaline to burn off energy
options.D: They stimulate the vagus nerve to activate the parasympathetic nervous system

explanation: Deep breathing acts like a brake pedal for your nervous system, stimulating the vagus nerve to switch you from 'fight-or-flight' to 'rest-and-digest.' [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h7)

question: Why should nurses care about a patient complaining of excessive gas?

options.A: It guarantees the patient has an active gastrointestinal infection.
options.B: It is a primary cause of severe malnutrition in hospital patients.
options.C: It always indicates a life-threatening bowel obstruction requiring surgery.
options.D: It can severely impact the patient's daily quality of life and social comfort.

explanation: While it's usually not dangerous, gas can cause a lot of embarrassment and discomfort. Being empathetic helps put your patients at ease!

question: What are the three classic signs of Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.A: Chest pain, high fever, and skin rash
options.B: Tremors, stiffness, and slow movement
options.C: Eye problems, poor balance, and confusion
options.D: Severe headache, stiff neck, and sudden paralysis

explanation: Great job! Watch out for trouble with eye movements, unsteady walking, and confusion—they form the classic triad.

question: A patient with gallbladder trouble feels pain up near their right shoulder blade. What is this called?

options.A: Referred pain
options.B: Phantom pain
options.C: Rebound tenderness
options.D: Somatic pain

explanation: Referred pain happens when internal organs and skin areas share the same spinal cord pathways, tricking the brain into feeling the pain somewhere else.

question: Why are people with long-term leg swelling at higher risk for skin infections like cellulitis?

options.A: Swollen legs attract insects that transmit bacterial infections.
options.B: Increased blood flow carries too many white blood cells to the skin.
options.C: Fluid buildup inside the tissues directly manufactures harmful bacteria.
options.D: Stretched, fragile skin easily develops cracks that let bacteria enter.

explanation: Exactly! When skin is constantly stretched out by fluid, it gets dry, thin, and fragile. Tiny cracks form easily, giving bacteria an easy doorway in.

question: What acid-base imbalance can develop from continuous stomach suctioning?

options.A: Metabolic acidosis
options.B: Respiratory acidosis
options.C: Metabolic alkalosis
options.D: Respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Sucking out large amounts of acidic stomach fluid leaves the body with excess base, leading to metabolic alkalosis. You're mastering body chemistry!

question: What is a common complication directly caused by skin traction straps and boots?

options.A: Permanent overgrowth of bone callus
options.B: Total loss of joint flexibility forever
options.C: Skin breakdown and pressure ulcer formation
options.D: Severe infection inside the bone marrow

explanation: Constant pressure from boots and tapes can easily irritate the skin. That's why regular skin checks are a nurse's best friend!

question: Why do patients living with HIV take a combination of multiple antiretroviral drugs instead of just one?

options.A: To prevent the virus from quickly developing drug resistance
options.B: To completely cure the virus within a few weeks
options.C: To prevent the drugs from causing any side effects
options.D: To make the pills easier to swallow every morning

explanation: Great thinking! HIV changes shape very easily. Using a combination of drugs that attack the virus from different angles stops it from mutating and overpowering the treatment.

question: What is the medical term for the complete absence of menstrual bleeding?

options.A: Amenorrhoea
options.B: Oligomenorrhoea
options.C: Dysmenorrhoea
options.D: Menorrhagia

explanation: Amenorrhoea literally means the absence of monthly flow, while the other terms describe painful periods, heavy bleeding, or infrequent cycles. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h1)

question: A community health nurse notices several children from different families coming in with the exact same pesticide poisoning signs. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Advise the local schools to close down all science laboratories
options.B: Treat the children and assume it is an isolated domestic accident
options.C: Wait until the end of the year to write a formal summary report
options.D: Report the cluster to public health authorities for investigation

explanation: You've got it! When multiple cases point to a shared source, alerting public health authorities right away helps track down the cause and protect the whole neighborhood.

question: Which gland is responsible for releasing the main growth hormone that helps children grow taller?

options.A: Exocrine pancreas gland
options.B: Anterior pituitary gland
options.C: Posterior pituitary gland
options.D: Adrenal cortex gland

explanation: Great recall! The anterior pituitary gland pumps out growth hormone, which teams up with other hormones to stretch those bones and build tissues during childhood.

question: How does low blood oxygen (hypoxia) affect an injured or swollen brain?

options.A: It helps the brain rest and heal faster from trauma
options.B: It has no real effect on brain tissue recovery
options.C: It lowers intracranial pressure back to normal levels
options.D: It worsens brain tissue damage and increases swelling

explanation: Oxygen is food for the brain! Starving delicate brain cells of oxygen causes more cells to die and makes the swelling much worse.

question: A patient with a stomach ulcer suddenly gets a hard, board-like tummy and severe pain. What likely just happened?

options.A: A blocked feeding tube
options.B: Mild constipation
options.C: The ulcer burst (perforation)
options.D: Normal gas buildup

explanation: A rigid, board-hard belly is a classic red flag for peritonitis—meaning stomach contents leaked into the belly cavity because the ulcer tore through. This is an emergency!

question: How can a nurse prevent nose tissue damage in a patient with a long-term nasogastric tube?

options.A: Leave the tape loose so the tube slides freely in and out
options.B: Reposition and tape the tube carefully to avoid pressure on the nostril edge
options.C: Apply thick antibiotic ointment over the entire face every hour
options.D: Push the tube an inch deeper into the nose twice a day

explanation: Relieving constant pressure against one side of the nostril prevents blood flow restriction and tissue death. Excellent clinical thinking!

question: Why do cat bites easily cause deep joint or tendon infections?

options.A: Cats secrete a local anesthetic that hides the pain of the bite
options.B: Cat saliva naturally resists all standard antibiotic treatments
options.C: Cat teeth are sharp and slender, pushing bacteria deep into tight tissues
options.D: Cats possess venom glands located near their salivary ducts

explanation: Think of a cat's teeth like tiny needles. They puncture deep beneath the skin, depositing bacteria right into sterile spaces like joints and tendons.

question: What is the medical term for a testicle that fails to move down into the scrotum?

options.A: Cryptorchidism
options.B: Hypospadias
options.C: Phimosis
options.D: Hydrocele

explanation: Cryptorchidism simply means the testicle didn't make the normal journey down into the scrotum before birth. You are doing great mastering these terms!

question: A patient recovering from a bacterial gut infection comes back weeks later with painful, swollen joints. What is this likely called?

options.A: Septic joint infection
options.B: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.C: Reactive arthritis
options.D: Osteoarthritis

explanation: Spot on! The joints 'react' to the earlier gut infection with inflammation. You are really mastering these tricky complications!

question: Why does a hurt or infected part of the body become warm and swollen?

options.A: Destruction of local nerve endings by invading bacteria
options.B: Decreased cellular activity slowing down the local metabolism
options.C: Rapid clotting of blood inside the deep muscle layers
options.D: Increased blood flow and fluid movement into the tissue

explanation: Correct! When your body sends extra blood and fluid to fight a germ at an injury site, it naturally causes warmth, redness, and swelling.

question: When does most of the myelination (insulation) happen in the human nervous system?

options.A: Only after a person reaches full physical adulthood
options.B: Immediately before the neural tube closes
options.C: Starting late in fetal development and continuing into adolescence
options.D: Exclusively during the first three weeks of embryonic life

explanation: Exactly! Myelination starts before birth for basic tasks, but it keeps going all through childhood and into our teenage years.

question: What is drug tolerance?

options.A: Rapid excretion of medicine by healthy kidneys
options.B: An allergic reaction occurring on first exposure
options.C: A reduced response to a drug after repeated use
options.D: The complete inability of a drug to bind receptors

explanation: Tolerance happens when your body gets too used to a medicine over time, meaning you might need a bit more of it to get the same effect.

question: Which dietary habit is most likely to trigger a painful gout flare?

options.A: Consuming large amounts of fresh leafy green vegetables
options.B: Eating heavy portions of red meat and drinking beer
options.C: Using low-sodium table salt on regular home-cooked meals
options.D: Drinking several glasses of plain water throughout the day

explanation: You've got this! Red meat and alcohol (especially beer) are high in purines, which spike uric acid levels and make it harder for the kidneys to clear them.

question: What makes an auto-disable syringe special?

options.A: Measure the exact weight of the patient receiving the drug
options.B: Automatically mix powdered medication with sterile water
options.C: Dissolve completely in water after a few minutes
options.D: Prevent the syringe from being used more than once

explanation: Auto-disable syringes have a clever built-in block that jams the plunger after one use, making accidental or intentional reuse impossible.

question: What is the main goal of community programs that prevent adolescent substance use?

options.A: Isolating teenagers from their peer groups completely
options.B: Stopping substance abuse before experimentation begins
options.C: Imposing harsh criminal punishments on drug users
options.D: Closing down all local pharmacies and stores

explanation: You nailed it! Prevention is all about stepping in early with healthy coping skills and support before drug use ever starts.

question: What is the main difference between a spontaneous abortion and an induced abortion?

options.A: Induced abortions happen completely by accident
options.B: Induced abortions are always caused by chromosomal defects
options.C: Spontaneous abortions only occur during the third trimester
options.D: Spontaneous abortions happen naturally without outside intervention

explanation: A spontaneous abortion (miscarriage) happens on its own due to natural factors, while an induced abortion is brought on by intentional medical or surgical steps. Simple and clear!

question: How will expanding advanced nursing roles mostly help rural communities?

options.A: By replacing all traditional community leaders with trained nurses
options.B: By lowering the total population growth rate in villages
options.C: By improving access to primary healthcare services in underserved areas
options.D: By eliminating the need for any pharmaceutical medications

explanation: Right! Advanced nurses help bridge the gap by bringing essential healthcare right to villages where doctors are scarce.

question: What is an important nursing check before preparing an infant for a scheduled circumcision?

options.A: Starting an intravenous line in the foot
options.B: Checking when the baby last fed
options.C: Shaving the entire pubic and scrotal hair
options.D: Administering a full dose of oral antibiotics

explanation: Checking the last feeding time helps prevent the baby from vomiting and potentially choking (aspirating) while being handled during the procedure.

question: Which discovery marked the beginning of the antibiotic era in the 20th century?

options.A: Aspirin
options.B: Morphine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Penicillin

explanation: Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin opened the antibiotic era, providing a powerful weapon against deadly bacterial infections. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why should you check if a patient has recently passed stool before giving a suppository?

options.A: Stool presence guarantees that the drug will be absorbed twice as fast
options.B: A full rectum can block the medication from contacting the mucosal wall
options.C: Bowel movements prevent the nurse from wearing disposable gloves
options.D: Empty bowels mean the patient is allergic to the prescribed drug

explanation: If the rectum is full of stool, the suppository won't touch the lining properly, reducing drug absorption.

question: Which of these materials must always be disposed of through incineration?

options.A: Office paper and envelopes
options.B: Clean cardboard shipping boxes
options.C: Anatomical and body parts
options.D: Plastic food water bottles

explanation: Correct! Anatomical waste requires complete thermal destruction via incineration for both sanitary safety and cultural respect.

question: Which key community figures can nurses partner with to encourage male involvement?

options.A: Commercial vehicle drivers
options.B: Secondary school prefects
options.C: Traditional rulers and religious leaders
options.D: International airline pilots

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders command great respect and can easily help shift community attitudes toward male participation.

question: What is the primary goal of routine screening tests like the Pap smear?

options.A: To permanently cure active bacterial infections in the pelvis
options.B: To detect abnormal cellular changes before cancer develops
options.C: To prevent the initial transmission of sexually transmitted germs
options.D: To measure hormone levels during the normal menstrual cycle

explanation: Pap smears catch weird cellular changes early—long before they turn into cancer—making treatment quick and easy.

question: What is the main cause of Maternal Depletion Syndrome?

options.A: Repeated, closely spaced pregnancies without adequate recovery time
options.B: A sudden genetic mutation triggered by multiple childbirths
options.C: Exposure to harsh environmental toxins during early adulthood
options.D: Consuming a diet high in processed foods during lactation

explanation: Maternal depletion happens when a mother's body doesn't get enough breathing room to heal and rebuild its nutrient stores between pregnancies.

question: Which test is usually ordered first to look for ovarian cysts or fibroids in the womb?

options.A: Abdominal X-ray
options.B: Magnetic resonance angiography
options.C: CT scan
options.D: Pelvic ultrasound

explanation: Well done! Pelvic ultrasound uses safe sound waves to give a clear picture of internal reproductive organs without using radiation.

question: You ask a patient to touch their own nose and then touch your finger over and over. What are you testing?

options.A: Superficial pain perception
options.B: Cerebellar coordination
options.C: Cranial nerve vision
options.D: Deep tendon reflexes

explanation: The finger-to-nose test checks the cerebellum, which is the part of the brain that keeps your body movements smooth and coordinated.

question: A student spends 12 hours a day playing online games, skips meals, and is failing exams. What does this point to?

options.A: Internet Gaming Disorder
options.B: Acute social anxiety
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
options.D: Normal adolescent recreation

explanation: When gaming takes over someone's entire life and basic needs or responsibilities get ignored, it goes way beyond normal fun and fits Internet Gaming Disorder.

question: What is the best diagnostic test to confirm gout by spotting crystals directly?

options.A: Analysis of synovial fluid via arthrocentesis
options.B: Routine complete blood count with differential
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging of the affected limb
options.D: Measurement of fasting serum glucose levels

explanation: Doctors confirm gout by drawing a small sample of fluid from the joint (arthrocentesis) and looking at it under a microscope to spot the crystals.

question: Why does a lack of proper sharps containers increase occupational hazards for nurses?

options.A: It reduces the shelf life of injectable antibiotics.
options.B: It causes patients to develop allergic reactions to metal needles.
options.C: It forces staff to handle loose needles and increases the risk of needle-sticks.
options.D: It prevents the hospital from purchasing intravenous fluids.

explanation: Without puncture-resistant safety boxes nearby, nurses face a much higher chance of accidental needle-stick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h5)

question: How can gender inequality play an indirect role in maternal mortality?

options.A: By altering the chromosomal makeup of the developing fetus
options.B: By speeding up the natural labor process to unsafe levels
options.C: By directly causing sudden postpartum hemorrhage after delivery
options.D: By depriving women of decision-making power over their own health and finances

explanation: That's correct. When women lack a voice in household decisions or money, they might struggle to get timely permission or funds to go to the clinic during an emergency.

question: What happens as a normal body reflex when a patient is given a direct-acting vasodilator?

options.A: Profound bradycardia
options.B: Severe bronchial spasm
options.C: Reflex tachycardia
options.D: Significant hypokalemia

explanation: Spot on! When blood pressure drops suddenly from a vasodilator, your nervous system panics a bit and speeds up the heart to compensate.

question: Which condition causes facial swelling, neck vein bulging, and trouble breathing due to a blocked major vein?

options.A: Spinal Cord Compression
options.B: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome
options.C: Febrile Neutropenia
options.D: Tumor Lysis Syndrome

explanation: When a tumor presses on the superior vena cava, blood gets backed up in the upper body, causing that distinct facial swelling. Spotting this makes you a sharp nurse!

question: What is a common belief among patients that drives the overuse of injections in many communities?

options.A: Oral medications have no side effects at all
options.B: Syringes contain vitamins that protect against malaria
options.C: Injections are more potent and work faster than oral drugs
options.D: Pills are more expensive than intravenous infusions

explanation: Many patients genuinely believe that if medicine isn't injected into their skin or veins, it's just 'too weak' to cure them. Patient education is our superpower here!

question: You see a colleague pouring leftover liquid antibiotics down the hospital sink. What is the right nursing response?

options.A: Help pour the remaining bottles down the drain to finish faster
options.B: Stop the colleague and explain proper pharmaceutical waste disposal
options.C: Throw the empty glass bottles into the general household trash bin
options.D: Ignore the action since liquid drugs dissolve safely in water pipes

explanation: Fantastic clinical judgment! Pouring medications down regular drains pollutes local water systems. Proper disposal protects both our patients and our environment.

question: A patient arrives at the clinic complaining of sudden crushing chest pain, sweating, and nausea that does not go away with rest. What condition should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Myocardial infarction
options.B: Stable angina pectoris
options.C: Chronic heart failure
options.D: Simple muscle strain

explanation: Severe crushing chest pain with sweating and nausea that persists at rest points strongly toward a heart attack. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h4)

question: Where should a nurse look first to confirm which diluent is safe for a specific powdered medication?

options.A: The nursing station whiteboard schedule for the current shift
options.B: The patient's daily food and fluid intake preference chart
options.C: The general hospital cleaning and sanitation protocol manual
options.D: The official drug manufacturer package insert or pharmacy reference

explanation: The manufacturer package insert or hospital pharmacy guide provides precise instructions on approved diluents and safe mixing ratios. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h2)

question: Why should a user hold their diaphragm up to the light before using it?

options.A: To check for small tears or holes that would let sperm pass through
options.B: To ensure the correct color coding for the specific menstrual cycle
options.C: To activate the chemical properties of the embedded spermicide
options.D: To warm up the silicone material for more comfortable insertion

explanation: A quick visual check against the light helps catch tiny punctures before they lead to an unplanned pregnancy. Simple and smart!

question: Why do we use barium sulfate during a barium meal X-ray test?

options.A: To act as a contrast medium on X-rays
options.B: To neutralize excess stomach acid
options.C: To numb the lining of the stomach

question: Why is the nursing process so helpful when caring for patients with blood disorders?

question: Why does the anaesthetist stay close to the patient's head during surgery?

question: Why are daily full-body soap baths usually not recommended for frail elderly patients?

question: Why must hospital menus in Nigeria include familiar local food staples?

question: At what exact moment during theatre proceedings is the 'Time Out' safety check done?

question: Which helpful cell in the central nervous system acts like a little garbage collector, clearing away germs and dead tissue?

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge faced in everyday rehabilitation nursing?

question: Why must community health nurses look beyond basic medical treatment to be effective advocates?

options.B: Because social and economic conditions heavily influence overall health outcomes

question: Which medical device or line should generally be left in place on a body after death if a coroner's investigation is required?

question: What are the two major muscle problems seen in a patient with achalasia?

question: A client with diabetes calls the clinic feeling nauseous and vomiting with a mild fever. What is the best advice to give them?

question: What is the primary role of the nurse during the implementation phase?

question: What is the main difference between routine blood typing and a cross-match?

question: Why must an antiseptic skin prep air-dry completely before inserting an IV catheter?

options.D: To keep the patient from feeling a burning sensation

question: Why is it risky to diagnose a nutrition problem based only on lab test results?

options.A: Patients refuse to provide samples for repeated nutritional screening.

options.C: Many non-nutritional factors like hydration and disease skew the results.

question: What do we call a nurse's ability to understand and respect a patient's cultural beliefs while giving great care?

options.A: Cultural competence
options.B: Clinical detachment

question: Why do nurse researchers submit a proposal before starting any study?

options.A: To recruit patients for immediate bedside treatment
options.B: To replace standard hospital nursing policies

options.D: To publish final clinical results quickly

question: What emotional feeling do patients adjusting to a new stoma most commonly experience?

question: Why is it important to listen to heart sounds using both the bell and the diaphragm of the stethoscope?

explanation: The diaphragm is best for high-pitched sounds like S1 and S2, while the bell is designed to capture low-pitched sounds like certain murmurs and gallops. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which seasonal weather condition in northern Nigeria is famous for triggering outbreaks of cerebrospinal meningitis?

options.A: The dry harmattan season

options.D: The coastal flooding period

question: Why is watching a patient walk (a gait assessment) so important for nurses?

options.C: It measures the exact lung capacity of the patient
options.D: It tests the cranial nerves inside the brain

explanation: Watching how someone walks tells you a lot about their balance and muscle strength, helping you keep them safe from accidental falls.

question: A patient goes home with a PICC line for long-term IV antibiotics. Why use a central line here?

options.A: It safely accommodates prolonged, concentrated intravenous drug therapy outside the hospital

options.C: It allows nurses to directly irrigate the bone marrow every few minutes

question: Why do public health experts say that most maternal deaths are preventable?

options.A: Because traditional herbs can cure all pregnancy issues
options.B: Because pregnant women rarely develop severe complications

question: What is the main focus of a psychosocial assessment in neurologic nursing?

options.A: Measuring physical strength and nerve reflexes

question: Why should nurses actively ask patients about their mood instead of waiting for them to bring it up?

options.A: Patients with depression lose the ability to speak completely

options.C: Many patients keep feelings hidden due to social stigma

question: Why should you warn patients taking regular NSAIDs to steer clear of alcohol?

options.C: It drastically increases the risk of stomach bleeding and ulcers
options.D: It completely stops the pain-relieving action of the drug

question: If you find a patient's PMI shifted far to the left, what does that usually suggest?

options.A: Collapse of the right lung

options.D: Enlargement of the heart

question: Why is building an early, trusting relationship with an expectant mother so important for a nurse?

options.A: It ensures the mother will have a completely pain-free labor

question: Which of these is strongly linked to developing primary bone cancer later in life?

question: Why must a patient taking methotrexate for an ectopic pregnancy avoid folic acid supplements?

question: Why are pancreatic protein-digesting enzymes released in an inactive form like trypsinogen?

question: Why is trauma-informed care so crucial when managing a GBV survivor in an emergency setting?

question: What is the main purpose of a clinical guideline in nursing?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to healthcare access for youths in Nigeria?

question: You notice a primary family caregiver looks completely exhausted and tearful during visiting hours. What is your best nursing move?

question: What is the main reason immobile patients develop deep vein thrombosis (DVT)?

question: What is the main reason teenagers often avoid visiting standard healthcare clinics?

question: A patient is taking oral ferrous sulfate for iron deficiency. How should a nurse advise them to take it for best absorption?

question: What does an Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) test actually measure?

question: What is a core duty of a nurse-midwife in promoting safe motherhood?

question: What does 'primary hypertension' mean?
