options.A: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
options.B: Cervical cancer
options.C: Bacterial vaginosis
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Correct! The HPV vaccine protects against high-risk strains that can lead to cervical changes and cancer later in life.

question: What makes foetal hemoglobin different from adult hemoglobin?

options.A: It is produced exclusively in the placenta
options.B: It has a higher affinity for oxygen
options.C: It carries carbon dioxide instead of oxygen
options.D: It breaks down much faster in cold temperatures

explanation: Foetal hemoglobin grabs onto oxygen much more tightly, enabling the baby to extract oxygen from maternal blood. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h5)

question: During a routine check, what does a pale, dusky, or blue-purple stoma tell you?

options.A: Inadequate blood supply to the stoma tissue
options.B: Normal healing after belly surgery
options.C: Too much fluid intake by the patient
options.D: A properly sealed ostomy appliance

explanation: Spot on. Color changes like blue, purple, or paleness mean blood flow is blocked or low—this is a true surgical emergency!

question: What happens if a nurse chooses a stockinette that is too narrow for a patient's leg?

options.A: It will dissolve when the plaster gets wet
options.B: It can squeeze the limb and restrict blood circulation
options.C: It will automatically stretch to fit any size perfectly
options.D: It will fall off the leg before the cast is applied

explanation: An undersized stockinette acts like a tourniquet when stretched tightly over a limb, cutting off proper blood flow. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of using a surgical safety checklist in the labor ward?

options.A: To slow down emergency cesarean sections unnecessarily
options.B: To give doctors extra paperwork to fill out after work
options.C: To make sure vital safety steps are never skipped during care
options.D: To replace the need for professional nursing judgment

explanation: Checklists act as a memory aid to ensure critical safety checks are completed before, during, and after procedures. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h5)

question: A newborn is scheduled for circumcision, but you notice the urethral opening is on the underside of the penis. What should you do?

options.A: Report the finding and hold the procedure because the foreskin may be needed for future repair
options.B: Apply an antiseptic ointment and wrap the penis tightly in gauze
options.C: Proceed with the circumcision quickly before the doctor arrives
options.D: Reassure the mother that this is a normal variation

explanation: This condition is called hypospadias. Always hold off on circumcision and report it—surgeons actually need that extra foreskin tissue to reconstruct the urethra later!

question: A patient expresses deep regret over past actions and asks if God can ever forgive them. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Dismiss the worry because everyone makes mistakes
options.B: Tell the patient that nurses only handle physical medications
options.C: Advise the patient to stop thinking about the past
options.D: Acknowledge their concern and offer to connect them with a spiritual care provider

explanation: Spiritual distress is real pain. Acknowledging it and connecting them with a chaplain or spiritual leader gives them the holistic support they need.

question: A patient calls reporting a fever of 38.5°C and severe pelvic pain three days after a medical abortion. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: An ongoing uterine infection
options.B: An allergic reaction to ibuprofen
options.C: A normal side effect of mifepristone
options.D: A normal reaction to lingering hormones

explanation: Spot on! A lingering fever and severe pain days after the procedure can signal a uterine infection that needs a doctor's attention and antibiotics.

question: Where does the normal electrical spark for every heartbeat start?

options.A: Bundle of His
options.B: Atrioventricular node
options.C: Sinoatrial node
options.D: Purkinje fibers

explanation: The sinoatrial (SA) node is the heart's natural pacemaker, setting the steady rhythm for every beat you take!

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is for chronic diseases, while quarantine is for acute injuries
options.B: Quarantine uses medications, while isolation uses physical barriers only
options.C: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people
options.D: There is no difference; the terms mean the exact same thing

explanation: Easy to remember: Isolation is for those already sick, while quarantine is for healthy folks who were exposed and need to be watched.

question: Why are corticosteroid injections into an arthritic joint typically limited to only a few times a year?

options.A: The body quickly builds up an absolute immunity to the drug
options.B: Steroids instantly dissolve all the remaining bone spurs
options.C: Frequent injections can cause further damage to the joint cartilage
options.D: The medication permanently stains the skin around the joint

explanation: While steroid shots relieve inflammation fast, repeated use over time can actually weaken and break down the remaining cartilage inside the joint. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h5)

question: What does 'appropriate information' mean in the context of rational drug use?

options.A: Giving clear instructions to the patient on how to take the medicine
options.B: Reporting drug manufacturing errors directly to the national health ministry
options.C: Publishing treatment outcomes in international medical and nursing journals
options.D: Filing the patient medical folder in the correct hospital archive cabinet

explanation: Appropriate information ensures that patients understand how, when, and why to take their prescribed medications safely. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h2)

question: When is the right time to suction a patient who is on a ventilator?

options.A: Every hour on the hour strictly
options.B: Only when clinical signs indicate retained secretions
options.C: Immediately before every physician visit
options.D: Whenever the patient asks for it

explanation: Suctioning is rough on the airways and steals a bit of air. Always assess the patient first and only suction when you actually hear or see signs that they need it!

question: An Alzheimer's patient gets very confused every late afternoon. Which nursing action helps best?

options.A: Restrict all fluid intake after noon to prevent bathroom trips
options.B: Establish a calm, predictable daily routine with engaging daytime activities
options.C: Change the patient's daily care schedule constantly to keep them alert
options.D: Keep the room dark and quiet all day to encourage deep rest

explanation: Spot on! Predictable routines and daytime activities help prevent 'sundowning' (late-day confusion) by keeping them secure and engaged. Great care planning!

question: Why is the eardrum (tympanic membrane) such a great spot to check core body temperature?

options.A: It shares a blood supply with the brain's temperature center
options.B: It is completely protected from any room air
options.C: Earwax never affects the reading
options.D: It always shows the highest temperature on the body

explanation: The eardrum shares blood vessels with the hypothalamus (your body's thermostat), giving you a very true picture of core temperature.

question: What is 'moral distress' in nursing?

options.A: The physical exhaustion caused by working long shifts in the ward
options.B: Disagreements between nurses regarding shift schedules
options.C: The emotional pain of knowing the right action but being unable to perform it
options.D: The sadness a nurse feels when a patient passes away peacefully

explanation: Moral distress happens when you know clearly what is best for your patient in your heart and training, but hospital rules, doctors, or lack of resources stop you from doing it.

question: Why do you listen with a stethoscope (auscultate) before pressing on the tummy (palpate) during an abdominal exam?

options.A: Palpation can trigger bowel movements and change the sounds you hear
options.B: Patients find palpation relaxing before listening
options.C: Auscultation is always a faster procedure
options.D: Doctors require notes in that specific order

explanation: Great catch! Pressing on the tummy first wakes up the bowels and makes them noisy, which messes up your listening assessment. Always listen first!

question: A nursing unit spends much more money on medical supplies this month than the budget allowed. How is this situation called?

options.A: A favorable variance
options.B: An unfavorable variance
options.C: A capital surplus
options.D: A balanced revenue stream

explanation: When your expenses go higher than your budgeted plan, it's called an unfavorable variance and means you need to recheck your spending.

question: Why is it risky for a patient to ignore digestive warning signs like bleeding?

options.A: It permanently damages the teeth due to upward pressure from the gut.
options.B: It can delay the diagnosis of serious conditions like bowel obstruction or disease.
options.C: It will automatically cause the patient to develop severe food allergies.
options.D: It stops the liver from producing essential clotting factors.

explanation: Catching serious issues early is key. Ignoring red flags can mean waiting too long to treat a serious gut problem.

question: A client had a vasectomy yesterday and asks when he can go back to heavy lifting at work. What do you tell him?

options.A: Wait until your semen analysis proves you are sterile in three months
options.B: You can return to lifting heavy items immediately if you wear a support
options.C: Heavy lifting is fine as long as you take pain medication
options.D: Wait at least a week and check with your doctor first

explanation: Correct! Strenuous work should wait for about a week to avoid bleeding or swelling in the scrotum.

question: What is widely considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in any hospital?

options.A: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.B: Administering daily multivitamins
options.C: Changing bed linen every morning
options.D: Wearing sterile gloves for all tasks

explanation: Spot on! Good old-fashioned hand hygiene is your number one weapon against hospital-acquired infections.

question: Why do the testes hang outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To shorten the length of the vas deferens tube
options.B: To allow easier passage of urine through the urethra
options.C: To protect the internal organs from high abdominal pressure
options.D: To keep sperm production at a slightly lower temperature

explanation: Brilliant! Sperm cells need a temperature slightly cooler than normal body heat to develop properly. The hanging scrotum acts like a natural cooling system.

question: How do azole antifungal drugs stop fungi from growing?

options.A: By stopping the production of essential fungal proteins
options.B: By destroying the genetic material inside the fungal nucleus
options.C: By creating physical holes in the fungal cell wall
options.D: By blocking an enzyme needed to make ergosterol

explanation: Azoles block the factory worker (enzyme) that builds ergosterol. Without ergosterol, the fungus can't maintain its cell wall and dies.

question: What is the typical clinical effect of a beta-blocker drug?

options.A: Stimulation of digestive motility and saliva production
options.B: Decreased heart rate and lowered blood pressure
options.C: Constriction of peripheral blood vessels and pupils
options.D: Increased heart rate and dilated bronchial tubes

explanation: Beta-blockers block adrenaline from working on the heart, helping it beat slower and with less force. This is great for managing high blood pressure!

question: When checking a home for safety, which of these is a common physical hazard?

options.A: High white blood cell count
options.B: Elevated resting heart rate
options.C: Incorrect medication dosage
options.D: Loose floor rugs

explanation: Watch out for loose rugs! They are physical hazards that easily cause elderly patients to trip and fall at home.

question: Which of these blood-borne viruses is famously tough and can survive for days on environmental surfaces?

options.A: Malaria parasite
options.B: Tuberculosis bacterium
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Hepatitis B Virus

explanation: Hepatitis B is remarkably hardy outside the body compared to many other viruses, staying infectious for a surprisingly long time. Good thing we practice strict infection control!

question: What is the primary function of the innermost layer, the tunica intima?

options.A: Anchoring major blood vessels securely to nearby skeletal bones
options.B: Supplying oxygenated blood directly to the thick outer muscle layers
options.C: Generating rhythmic electrical impulses to contract the vessel wall
options.D: Providing a frictionless endothelial surface for smooth blood flow

explanation: The tunica intima features a slick endothelial lining that reduces cellular friction and prevents unwanted clotting inside healthy vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which macronutrient provides the highest number of calories per gram?

options.A: Fat
options.B: Protein
options.C: Water
options.D: Carbohydrate

explanation: Fats are the most energy-dense nutrient, supplying nine kilocalories for every single gram consumed. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h2)

question: Which change is a normal part of the aging process in the cardiovascular system?

options.A: Rapid expansion of arterial walls
options.B: Enlargement of heart valves
options.C: Stiffening of the blood vessels
options.D: Increased resting heart rate

explanation: Blood vessels naturally lose elasticity and become stiffer with age, which can lead to higher blood pressure. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the definitive treatment when acute foetal distress does not respond to conservative resuscitation?

options.A: Strict bed rest for the mother
options.B: Administration of oral antibiotics
options.C: Monitoring for another two hours
options.D: Emergency delivery of the foetus

explanation: If the baby remains starved of oxygen despite nursing interventions, the only way to save it is to deliver the baby promptly. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h6)

question: Why does regular physical activity keep our muscles healthy and strong?

options.A: It removes the need for dietary protein intake
options.B: It permanently increases the total number of muscle fibers
options.C: It maintains muscle protein synthesis and strength
options.D: It completely stops the normal aging process of bones

explanation: You've got this! Active muscle use stimulates protein building blocks and metabolic processes, keeping muscle fibers strong and preventing wasting.

question: What do we call inflammation of the middle layer of the eye, which includes the iris?

options.A: Keratitis
options.B: Conjunctivitis
options.C: Retinitis
options.D: Uveitis

explanation: You got it! Uveitis is inflammation of the uvea (the middle layer). It can cause a deep, aching pain and make the eyes very sensitive to light.

question: What kind of body cells do cytotoxic drugs attack the most?

options.A: Rapidly dividing cells
options.B: Slow-growing bone cells
options.C: Mature nerve fibers
options.D: Dormant fat tissues

explanation: You've got this! Cytotoxic drugs are designed to target and destroy cells that divide quickly, which is a main feature of cancer cells.

question: Which of these is a major reason for internal displacement, especially in Northern Nigeria?

options.A: Strict government urban zoning laws
options.B: Voluntary migration for university education
options.C: Widespread industrial factory closures
options.D: Armed insurgency and violence

explanation: Sadly, armed conflict and insecurity force many families to flee their homes and seek safety elsewhere within the country.

question: Why is continuous heart monitoring a must right after a successful defibrillation?

options.A: To ensure the patient stays awake during recovery
options.B: To verify that the defibrillator battery is still fully charged
options.C: To measure the exact electrical resistance of the skin
options.D: To catch early warning signs of recurrent arrhythmias or re-arrest

explanation: Just because the heart restarted doesn't mean they're out of the woods. These patients are very fragile and can easily slip right back into a dangerous rhythm.

question: Why does study design matter so much when reading clinical research?

options.A: Clinical trial design determines how many pages the final published article will have
options.B: Journal editors only publish articles that use qualitative interview methods
options.C: Statisticians only analyze data that comes from retrospective hospital records
options.D: Some designs, like randomized controlled trials, provide much stronger proof than others

explanation: Exactly! Not all studies are built the same. Strong designs like randomized trials help cut out bias and give us trustworthy proof.

question: What does 'mesial temporal sclerosis' mean in temporal lobe epilepsy?

options.A: Scarring and neuron loss in the hippocampus
options.B: A sudden blockage of the carotid artery
options.C: Bleeding into the ventricles of the brain
options.D: Inflammation of the outer brain lining

explanation: Think of mesial temporal sclerosis as scarring deep inside the temporal area (the hippocampus). This damage makes it easier for abnormal electrical storms to start. Keep pushing forward! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why are bronchodilators sometimes given along with antibiotics for a lung infection?

options.A: To dry up all fluid inside the chest cavity
options.B: To bring down the patient's fever
options.C: To directly kill the bacteria in the air sacs
options.D: To relax tight airways and make breathing easier

explanation: Bronchodilators relax the muscles around the breathing tubes, opening them up so air flows more smoothly.

question: Why should nurses encourage residents to do tasks for themselves whenever they can?

options.A: To punish residents who refuse to participate in group activities.
options.B: To allow nursing staff to take longer breaks during the day.
options.C: To prevent rapid physical deconditioning and preserve independence.
options.D: To reduce the total amount of paperwork required for the shift.

explanation: Encouraging self-care keeps muscles strong and helps residents hold onto their independence and confidence. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: What right does every participant have during a clinical research experiment?

options.A: To change the research questions whenever they want
options.B: To receive free lifetime medical care after the study
options.C: To choose which group they want to be placed in
options.D: To withdraw from the study at any time without penalty

explanation: Participation is completely voluntary, and patients can quit whenever they choose without affecting their regular hospital treatment. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why do doctors give tocolytic drugs to a mother in preterm labour?

options.A: To delay delivery for 48 hours to give steroids time to work
options.B: To permanently stop uterine contractions for the rest of the pregnancy
options.C: To cure any underlying bacterial infection causing the labour
options.D: To lower the mother's blood pressure back to normal levels

explanation: Think of tocolytic drugs as our 'pause button'—they buy crucial hours so life-saving steroids can help the baby's lungs. You are thinking like a real nurse!

question: In Nigerian reproductive health programs, what does the acronym PMTCT stand for?

options.A: Primary Medical Treatment for Chronic Tumors
options.B: Prevention of Mother-To-Child Transmission
options.C: Public Midwifery Training and Community Testing
options.D: Postnatal Management of Teenage Children and Teens

explanation: You got it! PMTCT programs focus on stopping HIV from passing from an infected mother to her baby during pregnancy, birth, or breastfeeding.

question: Which infant condition is Bryant's traction typically used to treat?

options.A: Spina bifida complications
options.B: Severe clubfoot deformity
options.C: Fractured clavicle from birth
options.D: Congenital hip dislocation

explanation: Bryant's traction gently lifts both of a baby's legs straight up in the air to help realign a dislocated hip. Nursing pediatrics made simple!

question: What is the best position to place a distressed, breathless patient into right away?

options.A: High Fowler's or sitting upright leaning forward
options.B: Left lateral recovery position
options.C: Flat on the back with legs elevated
options.D: Prone position with a pillow under the chest

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Sitting upright helps pull the diaphragm down, making it much easier for the patient to draw a breath.
